description: The 30 hand-labelled claims of eval/calibration/webforms-shop.json about the synthetic tests/fixtures/repos/webforms-shop fixture (RF-305, RF-1411): expected is Supported when the cited lines show what the claim says, Rejected when they contradict it or do not show it. Invented code, no employer data.

input.claim: The details page reads the item id from the request (query string, form fields or cookies) and loads the item through the catalogue service.
The details page shows the item's name and its price formatted as currency.
The quantity on the details page must be a whole number from 1 to 10; otherwise the page shows 'Quantity must be between 1 and 10.'

files.Catalog/Details.aspx:
<%@ Page Language="C#" CodeBehind="Details.aspx.cs" Inherits="ShopWeb.Catalog.Details" %>
<html>
<body>
  <form runat="server">
    <asp:Label ID="NameLabel" runat="server" />
    <asp:Label ID="PriceLabel" runat="server" />
    <asp:TextBox ID="QuantityBox" runat="server" />
    <asp:RangeValidator ControlToValidate="QuantityBox" MinimumValue="1" MaximumValue="10" Type="Integer" runat="server" ErrorMessage="Quantity must be between 1 and 10." />
    <asp:Button ID="AddButton" Text="Add to basket" runat="server" OnClick="AddButton_Click" />
  </form>
</body>
</html>

input.claim: Clicking 'Add to basket' does nothing when the page is not valid.
After a line is added to the basket, the user is sent to the checkout page.
The basket is kept in the session under the key 'Basket'.
The home page fills the catalogue grid only on the first load, not on a postback.
A search removes the spaces around the typed text before it filters the catalogue.
Choosing the 'Details' command on a grid row opens the details page of that row's item.
The checkout page requires an e-mail address.

files.Orders/Checkout.aspx:
<%@ Page Language="C#" CodeBehind="Checkout.aspx.cs" Inherits="ShopWeb.Orders.Checkout" %>
<html>
<body>
  <form runat="server">
    <asp:TextBox ID="EmailBox" runat="server" />
    <asp:RequiredFieldValidator ControlToValidate="EmailBox" runat="server" ErrorMessage="E-mail is required." />
    <asp:RegularExpressionValidator ControlToValidate="EmailBox" ValidationExpression="^[^@]+@[^@]+$" runat="server" ErrorMessage="Enter a valid e-mail." />
    <asp:DropDownList ID="ShippingList" runat="server" />
    <asp:Button ID="PlaceButton" Text="Place order" runat="server" OnClick="PlaceButton_Click" />
  </form>
</body>
</html>

input.claim: An e-mail address is accepted only when it has one or more characters other than '@', then an '@', then one or more characters other than '@'.

input.claim: When the basket is empty at checkout, the user is sent back to the home page.
Placing an order empties the basket in the session.
Express shipping adds a fee of 12 to the order number and every other shipping method adds a fee of 4.
The basket is a list in which each line holds an item id and a quantity.
The quantity is not limited from 1 to 10 but from 1 to 100.

input.claim: Placing an order sends a confirmation e-mail to the customer.
Orders are saved in a database table when they are placed.
Standard shipping costs 12 and express shipping costs 4.
The details page sends users who are not signed in to the login page.
The home page fills the catalogue grid on every request, including postbacks.
The basket is stored in a browser cookie.
The confirmation page loads the order from the database by its number.
Checkout checks the chosen shipping method against a list of allowed values and refuses any other.
A discount is applied to baskets of more than five items.
The catalogue service returns the items whose name contains the search term.
An invalid e-mail address empties the basket.
The details page shows a 'not found' message for an unknown item id.
